q: In an experiment, the PO4 groups of the phospholipids facing the lumen of the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) are labeled. If in the course of time, the ER buds off vesicles which fuse with the cell membrane, the label will be found:
why: The lumen side of the ER membrane becomes the inside face of a vesicle, and when the vesicle fuses with the plasma membrane that face ends up towards the extracellular fluid.
opts: on the PO4 groups of cell membrane facing extra cellular fluid.
on the PO4 groups of cell membrane facing cytosol.
only on inner lumen of ER.
on both inner and outer laminae of ER.

q:
Which of the following primarily contribute to the 'cytomembrane system' of a cell?
I. Endoplasmic reticulum
II. Vesicles
III. Microtubules
IV. Mitochondria
V. Golgi apparatus
why: The cytomembrane (endomembrane) system consists of membranes that exchange material through vesicles: ER, vesicles and Golgi. Microtubules are not membranes and mitochondria are not part of the vesicle-traffic system.
opts: I, II, III, IV and V

q:
A cDNA library is a population of bacterial transformants in which each mRNA isolated from an organism is represented in the cDNA form. Choose the correct sequence in an experiment of production of cDNA:
A. Processed mRNA
B. Treatment with RNAase
C. Addition of poly T primers
D. Addition of DNA polymerase I
E. Treatment with DNAase
F. Addition of Reverse transcriptase
G. DNA Template
H. DNA-RNA complex
why: Start with processed mRNA, anneal a poly-T primer, make the first cDNA strand with reverse transcriptase, degrade the mRNA with RNase, then make the second strand with DNA polymerase I.

q: Plant cell A has an osmotic pressure of 12 atm and is immersed in solution of 10 atm osmotic pressure. Another cell B has 10 atm osmotic pressure and is immersed in solution of osmotic pressure of 8 atm. Both the cells are allowed to come to equilibrium, then removed from their solution and brought in intimate contact. Assuming that there is no external influencing force, what will be the result?
why: At equilibrium each cell has the same water potential as its bathing solution, so A sits at about -10 atm and B at about -8 atm. Water moves towards the lower (more negative) potential, i.e. from B to A.
opts: There will be a net flow of water from A to B.
There will be net flow of water from B to A.
There will be no net flow of water.
Water will freely pass from A to B but not from B to A.

q:
A cell is fully turgid when:
(i) Psi_w = 0
(ii) Psi_p = 0
(iii) Psi_p = Psi_s (in magnitude)
(iv) Psi_w = Psi_s
why: At full turgor the pressure potential balances the solute potential, so the water potential becomes zero. Pressure potential is then at its maximum, not zero, and water potential does not equal the solute potential.

q:
The concentrations of solutes present in solution A, B, C and D are given below:
Solution A: 0.1 moles/L sucrose + 0.1 moles/L KCl
Solution B: 0.2 moles/L sucrose + 0.2 moles/L KCl
Solution C: 0.1 moles/L sucrose + 0.1 moles/L CaCl2
Solution D: 0.1 moles/L sucrose + 0.2 moles/L CaCl2
The decreasing order of osmolarity of the four solutions would be:
why: Count particles: sucrose gives 1, KCl 2 and CaCl2 3 per formula unit. A = 0.3, B = 0.6, C = 0.4, D = 0.7 osmol/L, so D > B > C > A.
opts: solution A > solution C > solution D > solution B
solution B > solution D > solution C > solution A
solution C > solution A > solution D > solution B
solution D > solution B > solution C > solution A

q:
The critical day lengths for 4 plants are as follows:
Plant A - 15.5 hrs.
Plant B - 15.5 hrs.
Plant C - 10.0 hrs.
Plant D - 9.5 hrs.
Plant A flowers when it receives 8.5 or more hours of darkness.
Plant B flowers when it receives a minimum of 15.5 hrs of light.
Plant C flowers when it receives less than 10 hrs of light.
Plant D flowers when it receives less than 9.5 hrs of light.
Which one is a long day plant?
why: A long-day plant flowers only when daylight is at or above a critical length. Only B needs a minimum of light hours; A needs a minimum of darkness and C and D flower with short light periods.

q:
Which of the following sequences explains the different steps followed by the common bread mold Mucor in obtaining nutrition?
1. Synthesis of hydrolytic enzymes -> movement of enzyme from cell into substrate -> digestion of substrate by enzyme -> absorption of products by cell.
2. Absorption of substrate molecules by cell -> synthesis of hydrolytic enzymes -> digestion of substrate by enzymes
3. Synthesis of hydrolytic enzymes -> absorption of substrate molecules into cell -> digestion of substrate by enzymes.
4. Synthesis of hydrolytic enzymes -> absorption of substrate molecules into cell in small vesicles -> movement of enzymes into vesicles -> digestion of substrate by enzymes
why: Fungi are absorptive heterotrophs: they secrete digestive enzymes outside, digest the food externally, and then absorb the small products.

q: A baby born to a diabetic mother sometimes shows signs of hypoglycemia for some period just after birth. This is due to:
why: The fetus of a diabetic mother is exposed to high glucose and raises its own insulin output; after birth the sugar supply stops but the high insulin persists, causing low blood sugar.
opts: utilization of sugar from baby's blood for its activities after birth.
increased fetal insulin level to counter excess sugar from mother.
reduced production of maternal insulin as a result of diabetes.

q:
Values of the total surface area of the gills (expressed in arbitrary units) per unit gram body weight of two types of fish are given below.
Fish I: 442
Fish II: 1725
Which of the following can be predicted from the data?
why: Gill area tracks oxygen demand: sluggish bottom dwellers need little gill surface, while active surface-dwelling fish need much more.
opts: Fish I is marine while II is a fresh water fish.
Fish I is a bottom dwelling fish and II is a surface dwelling fish.
Fish I is bony fish and II is a cartilagenous fish.
Fish I is with small body mass and fish II is with large body mass.

q: Carbonic anhydrase enzyme catalyses the bidirectional reaction CO2 + H2O <-> H2CO3. If the activity of this enzyme is compared between three animals - elephant, sheep and mouse, the likely trend would be:
why: Mass-specific metabolic rate, and hence CO2 production, is highest in the smallest animal, so the mouse needs the most carbonic anhydrase per unit tissue and the elephant the least.

q: In a family, a female child is diagnosed with a known genetic disorder. She has four unaffected brothers and sisters. Neither parent nor any of the four biological grandparents of the affected child has had the disease. The most likely genetic explanation is that the disease is inherited as:
why: An affected girl with unaffected parents means both parents are carriers. An affected daughter cannot arise from an unaffected father with X-linked recessive inheritance, and a dominant trait would show in a parent.

q: Three copies of chromosome 21 in a child with Down's syndrome have been analysed using molecular biology techniques to detect any possible DNA polymorphism with reference to different alleles located on chromosome 21. Results showed that out of 3 copies, two of the chromosomes of the child contain the same alleles as one of the mother's alleles. Based on this, when did the non-disjunction event most likely occur?
why: Two identical copies of one maternal chromosome means sister chromatids failed to separate, which happens in meiosis II. A meiosis I error would give two different maternal alleles.

q: The genotypes of a husband and wife are I^A I^B and I^A i. Among the blood types of their children, how many different genotypes and phenotypes are possible?
why: Children can be I^A I^A, I^A i, I^A I^B or I^B i: four genotypes, giving blood types A, A, AB and B, i.e. three phenotypes.

q: In sweet pea plants, the genes for pollen shapes and flower colour are linked, purple being dominant over red and long pollen grain being dominant over round. If a plant heterozygous for both these traits is mated with a plant homozygous dominant for flower colour and homozygous recessive for pollen shape, what will be the phenotype of F1 generation?
why: The homozygous dominant parent gives only the purple allele, so every offspring is purple. For pollen shape this is a test cross (Ll x ll), so half the offspring are round.
opts: All plants with purple flowers and half with round pollen.
All plants with purple flowers and round pollen.
Half the plants with red flowers and round pollen.
The result will depend on whether the two dominant genes are present on the same or different chromosomes.

q: Igf2 gene of mouse encodes for insulin like growth factor II. A mouse that carries two normal wild type alleles of this gene is normal in size, whereas a mouse that caries two mutant alleles is dwarf. One heterozygous male was crossed with a heterozygous female, both being normal sized. The ratio of normal to dwarf was 1:1 instead of the expected 3:1. When some of these F1 male dwarfs were mated with homozygous mutant female dwarfs, normal mice appeared in the following progeny. This can happen if the normal Igf2 gene got imprinted in parent during:
why: A 1:1 ratio and the reappearance of normal offspring from dwarf males show that the paternal copy is the active one and the maternal normal copy is silenced, which means imprinting occurs during egg production.

q:
Consider the following two situations:
Situation I: Bird 1 hatches and grows up to become adult -> mates twice in lifetime -> lays five eggs -> three of them survive.
Situation II: Bird 2 hatches and grows up to become an adult -> mates four times in lifetime -> lays six eggs -> one of them survives -> bird 2 lives twice as long as bird 1.
Mark the correct interpretation.
why: Evolutionary fitness is measured by surviving offspring, not lifespan or matings. Bird 1 leaves three surviving young and bird 2 only one.
opts: Natural selection is acting on bird 1 but not on bird 2.
Bird 1 is evolutionarily more fit than bird 2.
Natural selection is acting on bird 2 but not on bird 1.
Bird 2 is evolutionarily more fit than bird 1.

q:
Which of the following best depicts the evolutionary sequence of plant characters?
1. Transition to land habitat
2. Evolution of seeds
3. Evolution of fruits
4. Evolution of vascular structures
why: Plants first moved onto land, then evolved vascular tissue, then seeds (gymnosperms), and finally fruits (angiosperms).

q: Some bird species follow army ants which walk on the forest floor. As the army ant colony travels on the forest floor, they stir up various flying insect species. As the insects flee from the army ants, the birds following the ants catch the fleeing insects. The type of interaction between the army ants and birds (I) and the birds and insects (II) respectively is:
why: The birds benefit from the flushed insects while the ants are unaffected, which is commensalism; the birds eating the insects is predation.

q:
A study of phytoplanktons was undertaken at the Gotri reservoir, which has a maximum capacity of 12 x 10^8 lit. The quantity of water in the reservoir and the planktonic density were estimated 4 times a year.
Month: August | November | February | May
Volume (lit): 12 x 10^8 | 10 x 10^8 | 2 x 10^8 | 9 x 10^5
Density (per ml): 8 | 11 | 21 | 25
In which month is the reservoir least productive?
why: Total plankton = density x volume. In May the volume is only 9 x 10^5 L, so even with the highest density the total plankton is far smaller than in other months.

q: "Living fossils" are the:
why: A living fossil is a lineage that survives today essentially unchanged in form from its ancient ancestors, such as coelacanth or Ginkgo.
opts: organisms that are long extinct but their DNA is accessible for study.
organisms that have become fossilized recently and all the structural proteins are not yet completely denatured.
ancient organisms persisting to modern times without any morphological changes.
ancient organisms persisting to modern times with gradual morphological changes.

q: In a lung cancer cell line, it is observed that a single point mutation (cysteine to phenylalanine) makes a protein defective in phosphorylation function. The loss of function is most likely due to:
why: Cysteine to phenylalanine changes the side chain's size and properties, most likely altering the protein's shape needed to interact with partners. Phenylalanine is hydrophobic and uncharged, so the solubility and charge options do not fit.
opts: increase in solubility of the protein in aqueous environment.
alteration of protein conformation essential for protein-protein interaction.
increase in the net charge of the protein leading to loss of active site.
decrease in hydrophobic interactions of the protein with other proteins.

q:
Which of the following proteins are likely to be active during mitosis?
i. Telomerase
ii. Primase
iii. Topoisomerase
iv. Kinesin
why: Telomerase and primase work in S phase DNA synthesis. During mitosis topoisomerase helps untangle condensed chromosomes and kinesin motors move spindle components and chromosomes.

q: A tuberculosis patient died within a few minutes of second intravenous administration of streptomycin and the post-mortem report gave anaphylactic shock as the cause of death. This is explained as:
why: Anaphylaxis is a type I hypersensitivity: IgE from the first exposure sits on mast cells, and the second dose triggers mass histamine release, vasodilation and a collapse in blood pressure.
opts: a sudden surge in IgM synthesis leading to complement activation causing fatal drop in blood pressure.
a vigorous precipitation of soluble antigens in body fluids triggered by the IgA insurgence leading to blockage of capillaries to vital organs.
IgE induced mast cell degranulation triggering abrupt dilation of peripheral blood vessels resulting in a precipitous drop in blood pressure.
IgD induced agglutination of antigen-bearing cells in vital organs leading to multi-organ failure.

q:
Apoptosis is programmed cell death characterized by the formation of apoptotic bodies whereas necrosis is characterized by bursting of cells. Which of the following condition/s lead/s to necrosis?
i. Gaps and nicks formed in DNA during replication cannot be repaired.
ii. Developing neurons fail to make synapses with neighbouring cells.
iii. Heart muscle cells damaged by oxygen depletion followed by cardiac infarction.
why: Necrosis is death from acute injury such as loss of oxygen in an infarct. Unrepaired DNA damage and failure of neurons to form synapses trigger programmed cell death (apoptosis).

q:
A few statements regarding the sexual and asexual modes of reproduction in plants are given.
1. In sexual reproduction, progeny are genetically different from each other.
2. In asexual mode of reproduction, progeny are genetically identical to each other but different from the parent.
3. Sexual reproduction is more conducive for driving evolution.
4. A minor change in the habitat may adversely affect all offspring derived by asexual reproduction.
5. A bisexual plant grown in isolation is always incapable of sexual reproduction.
Which of these statements are correct?
why: Sexual reproduction creates variation (1, 3), and genetically uniform asexual clones are all vulnerable to the same change (4). Statement 2 is wrong because clones match the parent, and 5 is wrong because a bisexual plant can self.

q: Which one of the following plant traits is NOT associated with colonization on land from aquatic habitat?
why: Land plants evolved apical meristems, protected multicellular embryos and gametangia, and all of them have alternation of generations, so its absence is not a land-colonisation trait.
opts: Production of gametes within multicellular organs.

q: Fluid filtration across capillaries depends on several factors. Which of the following causes net filtration at the arterial end and net reabsorption at the venous end?
why: Hydrostatic pressure falls along the capillary while plasma colloid osmotic pressure stays about constant, so outward pressure wins at the arterial end and inward osmotic pull wins at the venous end.
opts: Greater osmotic pressure of plasma at the arterial end of capillary than that at the venous end.
Greater interstitial fluid osmotic pressure at venous end of capillary than that at arterial end.
Greater capillary hydrostatic pressure than osmotic pressure of plasma at arterial end and the same being lower than plasma colloidal osmotic pressure at venous end.
Sum total of plasma colloidal osmotic pressure & interstitial fluid osmotic pressure at venous end being greater than the sum total at the arterial end capillary.

q:
Two statements regarding evolution are made below.
I. Rates of evolution are typically very slow because natural selection is usually ____P___ selection.
II. The plant population growing on high-zinc-soil is able to grow at concentrations which are otherwise lethal to plants of the same species. This is ____Q____ selection.
P and Q refer to:
why: Most of the time selection keeps the population near its optimum (stabilizing), which slows change. A population shifting towards zinc tolerance is moving in one direction, so that is directional selection.

q: Two alleles are found in Calico cats for coat color and are located on the X chromosome. One allele is responsible for black color while the other for orange color. Which of the following is correct about the phenotype of Calico cats?
why: Random X-inactivation in heterozygous females makes patches of cells expressing black or orange, giving a mosaic. Males have one X so can be either colour, and daughters depend on the father's X too.
opts: All male cats will have the same coat color.
Female cats can have mosaic pattern.
All females will show intermediate coat color.
All female cats born to mothers with black coat color will have black coat color.

q:
Which of the following properties of plasmids are central to the evolution of bacteria?
i. Plasmids are genetically dispensable for host cells in the absence of a selection pressure.
ii. Some plasmids have the ability to get transferred horizontally from one cell to another.
iii. Some plasmids permit interaction between bacterial cells of different species.
iv. Plasmids are naked DNA molecules incapable of survival outside a living cell.
why: What matters for bacterial evolution is that plasmids move genes horizontally, including between species (ii, iii). Being dispensable or unable to survive outside a cell does not drive evolution.

q: Bacteriophages take control of the host transcription machinery and sequentially express different groups of phage genes. A, B, C and D are four groups of phage genes expressed in the order A, B, C, D. Each group of genes has a specific type of promoter, each of which requires a specific sigma factor to initiate transcription. The genes encoding sigma factors to transcribe group A and group D genes are located in:
why: The first (group A) genes must be read by an existing host sigma factor encoded by the bacterium, whereas later groups such as D need new sigma factors the phage supplies from its own genome.
opts: bacterial genome and phage genome respectively.
phage genome and bacterial genome respectively.

q: Which one of the following molecules is least likely to pass through the plasma membrane?
why: Small uncharged molecules (CO2, ethanol, acetone) diffuse across the lipid bilayer, while NaHCO3 is ionic and cannot.

q:
Which of the following adaptations help plants grow under a canopy?
I. Increasing the specific leaf area (ratio of leaf area to dry mass).
II. Increase in the chlorophyll a/b ratio in the light harvesting complex.
III. Reduced tillering (production of lateral shoots) if the plants belong to grass species.
IV. Elongation of petioles to enhance access to sunlight.
why: Shade plants use thin broad leaves, fewer lateral shoots and longer petioles to capture limited light. Shade adaptation raises chlorophyll b (lowers the a/b ratio), so II is wrong.

q:
The following characters are found in many trees that grow in temperate forests.
i. Pollen are shed at the beginning of growing season before the leaves develop.
ii. Shedding of pollen is timed to avoid high humidity and rain.
In such trees, the type of pollination is most likely to be:
why: Shedding pollen before leaves can block the air, and in dry weather, so that wind can carry it, points to wind pollination (anemophily).

q: During the growth of marine fish, initially, yolk sac and skin are the principal sites where transport protein "X" is located. Later, skin and gills become principal sites and finally 'X' becomes localized to gills. The protein "X" is:
why: Marine fish excrete excess salt through ion-transporting cells, first in the yolk sac and skin and later in the gills. The transporter doing this is the Na+/K+ ATPase; the other options are not ion-regulation transporters.

q:
Consider a case where a mutation 'R' occurred in some prairie moles influencing their behavior/physiology. In which of the following cases, it can be asserted that the mutant allele frequency will increase in the population?
i. The mutation results in enhanced monogamy.
ii. The mutation results in greater average number of surviving offspring as compared to the wild type population.
iii. The mutation results in longevity in the mole population.
iv. The mutation results in greater average time spent together by paired male and female moles compared to the wild type population.
why: An allele spreads when its carriers leave more surviving offspring (fitness). Monogamy, longer life or time spent together do not by themselves guarantee more offspring.

q:
The wild type lac operon is inducible. Mutations in the operator region (OC) can make the operon constitutive, i.e. the operon is active even in the absence of the inducer such as lactose. Constitutive expression can also be observed if the lac repressor is not synthesized. Partial diploids (merodiploids) can be developed in E. coli by transforming E. coli with a plasmid carrying a genomic DNA fragment. Of the following genotypes of merodiploids which one of them would show constitutive expression of the lac operon resulting in synthesis of functional proteins?
[delta-I: deletion of lac I gene, I+: wild type lac I gene, lac Z-, Y- & A-: mutated lac Z, Y & A genes, lac Z+Y+A+: wild type lac Z, Y & A genes, OC: operator constitutive mutant, O+: wild type operator]
why: OC acts only in cis, so constitutive expression needs OC on the same DNA as functional Z, Y, A genes. Only option c has that; in d the OC copy carries mutant genes, and in a and b the repressor from I+ in trans still controls the operon.
opts: delta-I O+ Z+Y+A+ / I+ O+ Z+Y+A-
delta-I O+ Z-Y-A- / I+ O+ Z+Y+A+
I+ OC Z+Y+A+ / I+ O+ Z+Y+A+
I+ O+ Z+Y+A- / I+ OC Z-Y-A-

q: A set of genes that are linked to one another is called as a linkage group. The minimum number of linkage groups in an organism is equal to its haploid number of chromosomes. Which of the following events can change the linkage group of a given gene?
why: A gene changes linkage group only if it moves to a different chromosome, which is what a translocation does. Inversions and recombination rearrange genes within the same chromosome.

q: One can observe three phenotypic variants in the 4 o'clock plant, Mirabilis jalapa, namely, variegated leaves, green leaves and yellow leaves. If pollen from a branch that bore only variegated leaves fertilize ovules from a branch that had only green leaves, the leaves of the plantlets will be:
why: Leaf colour here is inherited through plastids, which come only from the egg cell (maternal inheritance). The ovules came from a green branch, so all progeny are green.

q:
Which of the following support/s common ancestry of Humans, Cheetah, Whale and Bat?
i. Homologous organs
ii. Analogous organs
iii. Vestigial organs
why: Homologous and vestigial structures reflect inheritance from a common ancestor, whereas analogous organs arise by convergent evolution and give no evidence of common ancestry.

q: When human genome was sequenced, the annotated number of genes was found to be ~20,000. Based on complexity of humans, however, it was expected that there would be more than 100,000 genes. Which of the following statements would explain this discrepancy?
why: Alternative splicing lets one gene produce several different mRNAs and proteins, so a modest gene count can still give a large proteome.
opts: The current methods of sequencing are inefficient to identify the large number of genes.
Enhanced somatic recombination in humans takes place to generate more number of genes.
Large number of genes in humans undergo alternative splicing to generate proteome diversity.
Fewer genes through frame shift translation can generate more number of proteins.

q: Consider a diploid organism with 2n value of 4. How many chromosomes and DNA molecules respectively are present in the G1 and G2 phases of a somatic cell of this organism? (consider only nuclear DNA)
why: Chromosome number stays 4 after replication because sister chromatids are still joined at the centromere, but each chromosome now has two DNA molecules, giving 8 in G2.

q: Of the sunlight that reaches the surface of the earth, biological processes mostly make use of light of wavelength between 400nm to 700nm. Which of the following transitions, critical for life, will occur in the molecules absorbing photons in this range of wavelengths?
why: Visible photons carry energies of about 1.8 to 3 eV, matching the gaps between electronic energy levels of pigments. Vibrational and rotational transitions need infrared or microwave photons.

q:
A scientist was analysing a particular DNA sequence in humans and its relation to a disease. Which of the following data is most supportive of the scientist's hypothesis that the particular sequence is NOT related to the disease?
Each option gives: percent of diseased individuals having the sequence / percent of non-diseased individuals having the sequence.
why: If the sequence is unrelated to the disease, it should occur about equally in both groups. Only 48% versus 52% shows no association.

q: Three siblings have the following blood groups: B Rh positive; A Rh negative; and O Rh positive. Based on this information what will be the parents' genotype for the two blood group loci? (Note: Rh positive allele is dominant represented by +.)
why: The A Rh-negative child needs a - allele from each parent, and the O child needs i from each, so both parents carry i and -. Only the pair B i (+-) and A i (--) can also give B and Rh-positive children.

q: In natural populations, individual allele frequencies are changing all the time. Several factors can be responsible for change in allele frequency. Among these, the only factor that produces adaptive evolutionary changes is:
why: Mutation, gene flow and drift change allele frequencies without regard to fitness; only natural selection systematically favours alleles that improve survival and reproduction.

q:
Intrinsic rate (r) of natural increase in number, generation time in days and net reproduction rate (R0) for 3 animals are given:
(i) r = 0.0125, average generation time 141.8, R0 5.9
(ii) r = 0.101, average generation time 55.6, R0 275
(iii) r = 0.111, average generation time 30.9, R0 30.9
(i), (ii) and (iii) most likely are:
why: The rat has the longest generation time and lowest r and R0. The beetle has a huge net reproductive output per generation (275), and the louse has the shortest generation time with moderate R0.

q:
The table shows the number of study sites predicted to be occupied or unoccupied by tigers, based on a mathematical model of their habitat use and the actual observed presence or absence of tigers in those study sites based on rigorous field surveys. Assuming the field studies are accurate:
Predicted present: observed present 26, observed absent 6.
Predicted absent: observed present 9, observed absent 43.
What percentage of all the study sites was correctly predicted by the habitat model?
why: Correct predictions are 26 + 43 = 69 out of 26 + 6 + 9 + 43 = 84 sites, which is about 82.1%.

q: Table of tiger habitat model results: predicted present: observed present 26, observed absent 6; predicted absent: observed present 9, observed absent 43 (assume the field studies are accurate). Which statement best describes the accuracy of the habitat model?
why: Of the sites with observed absence, 43 of 49 (88%) were predicted correctly, while of those with observed presence only 26 of 35 (74%) were. So absence was predicted better.
opts: The model was better at predicting tiger presence than tiger absence.
The model was better at predicting tiger absence than tiger presence.
The model equally good at predicting tiger presence and tiger absence.
The model was unable to predict either tiger presence or tiger absence.

q:
Lipid rafts are cholesterol-rich and glycosphingolipid-rich microdomains in the plasma membrane. Integral membrane proteins required for immune signaling and cell-cell communication are found in rafts. A few statements regarding lipid rafts are given below.
i. The raft microdomains are more fluid than rest of the membrane.
ii. Integral membrane proteins present in lipid rafts require a specific modification.
iii. The raft microdomains do not freely mix with rest of the membrane and can induce protein clustering.
iv. Lipid rafts help in preferential endocytosis of clustered signalling proteins.
Pick the combination of correct statements.
why: Cholesterol and sphingolipids pack tightly, making rafts more ordered and less fluid, so (i) is false and every option containing it is out. That leaves (ii) and (iii) as the combination the key accepts.

q:
A growth factor, promoting cell growth activates a distinct cascade of phosphorylation events mediated by protein kinase enzymes. The ATP dependant phosphorylation of the target by a kinase can regulate the function of target proteins. Several statements made in this regard are given below:
1) Energy released from ATP hydrolysis by the kinase helps in activation of the target protein.
2) ATP hydrolysis-mediated phosphorylation often brings structural changes in the target protein.
3) Phosphorylation can facilitate new protein-protein interactions to target proteins.
4) Phosphorylation of the target protein must activate it.
Which of the statements is/are true?
why: Adding a charged phosphate changes protein conformation and creates docking sites for other proteins (2, 3). The energy is not transferred to the target, and phosphorylation can inhibit as well as activate.

q: Toluidine is a metachromatic stain that can impart different colors to different plant tissues. The primary cell walls turn pink while secondary cell walls turn blue. Which of the following is likely to result?
why: Collenchyma, like chlorenchyma, has only primary walls (pink); xylem vessels have lignified secondary walls and would be blue.
opts: Collenchyma cell walls will turn pink.

q:
Select the correct combination of the following taxa which have been sequentially arranged in the order from most inclusive (most general) to least inclusive (most specific).
1) Insecta
2) Arthropoda
3) Hymenoptera
4) Ecdysozoa
5) Bilateria
6) Apis
why: Bilateria is the widest group, containing Ecdysozoa, which contains Arthropoda, then class Insecta, order Hymenoptera and genus Apis.

q: Which of the following statements best defines a portal system?
why: In a portal system (such as hepatic or hypophyseal portal) a vein drains one capillary bed and then breaks up into a second capillary bed before returning to the heart.
opts: Part of the circulatory system where arteries subdivide into large number of branches of capillaries and again join with another artery.
A system of blood supply between heart and liver.
A system of veins which begins and ends with a bed of capillaries.
Part of the lymphatic circulatory system found in higher chordates where blood from organs is forwarded to open sinus through a network of capillaries.

q: Which of the following structural modifications are NOT essential in terrestrial mammals for cursorial (rapid running) adaptation?
why: Runners have fewer digits, hinge-like joints restricting motion to one plane and fused long foot bones. Grasping, opposable digits are adaptations for climbing and handling, not running.
opts: Reduction in the number of digits and phalanges.
Modification for articulation of bones to restrict movement in one plane.
Fusion of bones of the sole and palm.

q:
The urine osmotic concentrations and urine/plasma salt concentration ratios for four animals (human, P, Q and R) are given in the table.
Human: urine max. osmotic concentration 1.4 osm/L, urine/plasma salt concentration ratio 4
P: 5.5, 14
Q: 3.1, 10
R: 0.52, 2
P, Q & R respectively most likely represent:
why: Desert kangaroo rats concentrate urine most (5.5), cats are also good concentrators, and the aquatic beaver has the weakest concentrating ability, even below humans.

q: Crossing-over is absent during meiosis in males of Drosophila melanogaster. At what stage of meiosis does segregation of alleles occur in these males?
why: Without crossing over, the two alleles of a gene lie on separate homologues and are separated when homologous chromosomes move apart in anaphase I.

q:
A Drosophila mutant that cannot fly is isolated in an Indian laboratory. The mutant phenotype is recessive and has been mapped to gene 'M'. Three European labs in UK, Spain and Germany independently isolated mutants with the same phenotype. In order to test if these mutants also resulted from mutation in gene 'M', the following crosses were made and the phenotype of the F1 progeny analyzed:
India x UK: cannot fly
India x Spain: can fly
India x Germany: can fly
UK x Spain: can fly
UK x Germany: can fly
Germany x Spain: cannot fly
Based on the above findings, which of the European mutants is most likely to map to gene "M"?
why: This is a complementation test: a cross that still cannot fly means both mutations are in the same gene. India x UK fails to complement, so UK is in gene M; Germany and Spain fail to complement each other but not India, so they share a different gene.

q:
Sea turtles show the following life history characteristics:
i. They live for many years.
ii. They produce massive number of eggs at a time.
iii. They show limited parental care.
Which of the following statements is true for sea turtles?
why: Long life is a K-trait, whereas huge numbers of eggs and little parental care are r-traits, so sea turtles combine both strategies.
opts: They show r-strategy because characters i and iii are typical of r - strategy of life history.
Sea turtles show K-strategy because characters i and ii are typical K -strategy of life history.
They show mixed K-r strategy as character iii is typical of a K-strategist while i and ii of r- strategist.
Sea turtles show mixed K-r strategy as feature i is observed in K-strategy while ii and iii are observed in r- strategy.

q:
An invertebrate possessing the following features was found in a sample collected from a freshwater ecosystem.
No antero-posterior axis
Presence of gastro-vascular cavity
No circulatory system
No organ system
The organism most likely is a:
why: Radial symmetry (no antero-posterior axis) with a gastrovascular cavity and no organ systems is the cnidarian body plan. Sponges lack a gut cavity, and flatworms and rotifers are bilateral.

q: Which of the following features is common to both cnidarians and platyhelminthes?
why: Both groups have an incomplete gut with one opening acting as mouth and anus. Platyhelminthes do have organ systems, and self-fertilisation or absorption are not common defining features.
opts: Digestive system with a single opening.
Ability to absorb nutrients across their body wall.

q:
Which of the following sets of chemicals and/or instrument can be used to prepare sodium phosphate buffer of approximately pH 7.0?
I. Na2HPO4 salt, NaH2PO4 salt and water.
II. NaH2PO4 salt, NaOH solution and pH meter.
III. Na2HPO4 salt, water and pH meter.
IV. Stocks of: NaH2PO4 solution, Na2HPO4 solution and water.
(pKa values for phosphoric acid: 2.12, 7.21, 12.32)
why: pH 7 lies near pKa2 (7.21), so a mixture of H2PO4- and HPO4(2-) works. Mixing the two salts (I), mixing the two stock solutions (IV), or partly neutralising NaH2PO4 with NaOH while monitoring pH (II) all give this pair; Na2HPO4 alone in water (III) is too basic and cannot be brought down to 7.

q:
A student was studying transport of a solute 'X' through the erythrocyte membrane in a laboratory. She obtained the following data:
Expt. I: [X] outside 0 mM, rate of entry of X 0 umoles/min
Expt. II: 0.5 mM, 7 umoles/min
Expt. III: 1.0 mM, 14 umoles/min
Expt. IV: 2.0 mM, 26 umoles/min
Expt. V: 3.0 mM, 35 umoles/min
Expt. VI: 5.0 mM, 38 umoles/min
Which of the following can be deduced from the observations?
why: The rate rises almost linearly at low concentration but levels off near 38 at high concentration, which is saturation kinetics typical of carrier-mediated transport. So the number of carriers limits the rate; simple diffusion would stay proportional.
opts: The experiments I - VI were carried out at successively increasing temperatures.
The nature of solute must be highly non-polar.
Increase of solute concentration outside has resulted in proportional increase in rate of entry of the solute into the cell.
The major limiting factor for the rate of entry is the carrier protein transporter.

q:
One of the oxygen utilizing enzymes, cytochrome P450 catalyzes the following reaction:
R - H + NADPH + H+ + O2 <=> R - OH + NADP+ + H2O
These enzymes are also found useful in detoxification of xenobiotics (chemicals foreign to an organism). Which of the following is the most likely mode of action of these enzymes?
why: The reaction adds an -OH group to the substrate (R-H becomes R-OH), which makes a hydrophobic xenobiotic more polar and water soluble, so it can be excreted.
opts: They create a non-reducing environment by utilizing NADPH, thus nullifying the effect of the xenobiotics.
They create anaerobic conditions in the cell by utilizing oxygen and thus decreasing the effect of the xenobiotics.
They convert the xenobiotics to its polar form, which is easy to be excreted.
They promote oxidative phosphorylation to generate ATP for detoxification of the xenobiotics.

q:
A dichotomous key for a few cell components is given below.
1a. Found in cytosol.....go to 2
1b. Found in nucleus....A
2a. Membrane-bound structure....go to 3
2b. Structure is not membrane bound...B
3a. Flattened sheet-like structure....go to 4
3b. Spherical or elongated structure....go to 6
4a. Smooth exterior.....go to 5
4b. Rough exterior......C
5a. Involved in lipid metabolism.....D
5b. Several spherical vesicles found in vicinity.....E
6a. Bound by single membrane....go to 7
6b. Bound by double membrane.........F
7a. Contains oxidative enzymes........G
7b. Contains hydrolytic enzymes.......H
E, F and G respectively most likely represent:
why: E is a smooth flattened membrane stack with vesicles nearby, i.e. the Golgi. F is a double-membrane spherical or elongated organelle, i.e. a mitochondrion. G is single-membrane with oxidative enzymes, i.e. a peroxisome.

q: Water movement via soil and within different parts of a plant can take place through various pathways. The major transport in the soil and through the cell walls respectively occur via:
why: Water moves through soil mainly by bulk flow, and within the plant the cell-wall route is by definition the apoplast pathway.

q: Secondary wall thickening and lignification of tracheids and vessels is considered an important adaptation for water transport because:
why: Water in xylem is under tension (negative pressure) from transpiration pull; rigid lignified walls stop the conduits collapsing inward, keeping the water column intact.
opts: lignification of the walls gives strength to tall plants.
the hydrophobic nature of lignin helps plants absorb water more efficiently.
strong lignin walls resist collapse of column structure which would result from high surface tension of water.
biodegradability of lignin being very low, it gives plants protection from various infections.

q: Phytoalexins are a type of oligosaccharin molecules which act as defense molecules in case of any pathogenic attack in plants. Which of the following is the correct sequence of attack and defense?
why: The fungus is the invader and uses its own pectinase to break the plant wall; the breakdown fragments (oligosaccharins) then trigger the plant cells to make phytoalexins.
opts: Fungal invasion of plant cells → Pectinase secreted by plant cells → Phytoalexins produced by plant cells.
Fungal invasion of plant cells → Chitinase secreted by plant cells → Phytoalexins produced by fungal cells.
Plant cell invades fungal body → Pectinase secreted by plant cells → Phytoalexins produced by plant cells.
Fungal invasion of plant cells → Pectinase secreted by fungal cells → Phytoalexins produced by plant cells.

q:
Which among the following physiological changes occur when plants experience drought?
(i) Accumulation of abscisic acid
(ii) Accumulation of solutes
(iii) Increased photosynthesis
(iv) Increased stomatal conductance
(v) Increased cell elongation
why: Drought raises ABA, which closes stomata, and cells accumulate solutes for osmotic adjustment. Photosynthesis, stomatal conductance and cell elongation all fall.

q: Among various types of digestive systems, horse exhibits a modified monogastric type of stomach and digestive system. The correct path of food in this type of digestive system is:
why: The horse is a hindgut fermenter: food passes the stomach and small intestine first, then enters the cecum, followed by the large colon, small colon, rectum and anus.
opts: Mouth → esophagus → stomach → small intestine → large colon → small colon → cecum → rectum → anus
Mouth → esophagus → stomach → small intestine → cecum → large colon → small colon → rectum → anus
Mouth → esophagus → cecum → stomach → small intestine → large colon → rectum → anus
Mouth → esophagus → cecum → small intestine → large colon → small colon → rectum → anus

q: Assume that independent orientation of chromosomes in meiosis and random union of gametes produced by male and female of a species are the only responsible factors for genetic variations in their offspring. If the diploid chromosome number of this species is 40, the number of possible combinations of chromosomes for their sperm / ovum is A^P and number of possible combinations of chromosomes for their offspring is B^Q, then values of A, B, P and Q would be:
why: With 20 chromosome pairs, each gamete has 2^20 possible chromosome combinations. Two random gametes unite, so the offspring have 2^20 x 2^20 = 2^40 combinations.

q: Consider a hypothetical species where meiotic cell division occurs after zygote formation. This organism is likely to be:
why: Meiosis after zygote formation (zygotic meiosis) means the zygote is the only diploid stage and the organism itself is haploid; fertilisation implies it reproduces sexually.

q: Genetic drift is a random fluctuation in allelic frequencies owing to the variations in reproductive fitness in populations. The chance of drift causing gene fixation is highest:
why: Random sampling error in allele frequencies is largest when few individuals reproduce, so alleles drift to fixation or loss fastest in small populations.
opts: when neutral genes are located near genes under selection.
when genes are under negative selection.

q:
Field capacity can be defined as the water content of a soil after it has been saturated with water and the excess water has been allowed to drain away. The field capacity of soil depends on the type of soil particles that make up the soil. The physical characteristics of different types of soils (I - IV) are given below.
Soil I: particle diameter 20 - 2 um; surface area per gm 10 - 100 m2
Soil II: particle diameter 200 - 20 um; surface area per gm < 1 - 10 m2
Soil III: particle diameter < 2 um; surface area per gm 100 - 1000 m2
Soil IV: particle diameter 2000 - 200 um; surface area per gm < 1 - 10 m2
Mark the correct statement.
why: Clay has the smallest particles (< 2 um) and the largest surface area, so it holds the most water against drainage; that matches soil III. The coarsest soil (IV) would be sand, not silt.
opts: III could be clayey soil with the maximum field capacity among I - IV.
I could be sandy soil with maximum field capacity among I - IV.
II could be sandy soil with least water retention capacity among I - IV.
IV could be silty soil with least water retention capacity among I - IV.

q: Alcock (1979) while studying reproductive strategies of Digger Bees (Centris pallida) identified two different strategies, patrolling and hovering. Patrolling involves activities such as finding virgin females buried in the nest, excavating them and mating with them. Excavation takes a few minutes during which there is a chance that other males might arrive resulting in violent fights. Hovering males, on the other hand, hover near flowering trees and wait for receptive females to fly by. Mating success is more in patrolling as compared to hovering. Which of the following statements is correct?
why: Patrolling pays more but involves violent fights, which large males are better able to win; small males do better by avoiding fights and hovering.
opts: Smaller males may prefer patrolling and larger males may prefer hovering to give tough competition for reproduction.
Larger males may prefer patrolling and smaller males may prefer hovering for better reproductive success.
All males irrespective of their size would prefer patrolling strategy for better reproductive success.
Larger and smaller males both may prefer hovering to avoid violent fights.

q:
Due to dynamic phosphorylation-dephosphorylation process, almost all signaling pathways are reversible and in many cases phosphorylation activates the signaling. Which combination of following conditions will inhibit such a signaling pathway in operation?
i. Application of kinase inhibitor.
ii. Treatment with a phosphatase inhibitor.
iii. Phosphorylated amino acid residue binder recruiting a phosphatase.
iv. Binding of a phosphorylated amino acid residue recognizing kinase.
v. An interaction stabilizing the half-life of the phosphorylated amino acid residue.
why: If phosphorylation switches the pathway on, anything that blocks the kinase (i) or brings in a phosphatase to remove the phosphate (iii) switches it off. Blocking phosphatases, recruiting another kinase or stabilising the phosphate would keep it on.

q:
Acquired immune system produces different types of antibodies upon exposure to an antigen. The type of antibody produced varies based on the time from the initial exposure to antigen, the duration after the initial exposure, and secondary or every subsequent exposure to the same antigen. A murine model was infected with a bacterial pathogen. Serological analysis was carried out to monitor the presence of antigen-specific IgM & IgG antibodies at different Days Post Inoculation (DPI) as shown in the table below.
Sample 1: DPI 1, IgM -, IgG -
Sample 2: DPI 7, IgM ++, IgG -
Sample 3: DPI 10, IgM +, IgG +
Sample 4: DPI 28, IgM -, IgG ++
Which of the sample number/s in the above table indicate/s an ongoing active infection condition?
why: IgM is the early antibody and marks a current infection. Samples 2 and 3 still have IgM (with IgG only starting in 3), whereas sample 4 has only IgG, indicating a past infection, and sample 1 has none.

q: 0.3 M sucrose and 0.3 M glycerol both show osmotic potential same as that found within a human erythrocyte. If RBCs are suspended in these solutions independently for about an hour, cells suspended in glycerol solution show hemolysis. Which of the following can be best deduced from this?
why: Both solutions are isotonic initially, so lysis in glycerol means glycerol slowly crosses the membrane; water then follows it in and the cell swells. Sucrose cannot cross, so it stays isotonic.
opts: Glycerol is more hydrophilic than sucrose.
Water from the glycerol solution enters the cells leaving a hypertonic solution of glycerol outside.
Glycerol has greater cell membrane permeability than sucrose.
Sucrose being a disaccharide requires a specific carrier protein to pass through the erythrocyte membrane.

q:
The neurotransmitter acetylcholine is made in the cytosol and then transported into synaptic vesicles, where its concentration is more than 100-fold higher than in the cytosol. When synaptic vesicles are isolated from neurons, they can take up additional acetylcholine added to the solution in which they are suspended, but only when ATP is present. Na+ ions are not required for acetylcholine uptake, but, curiously, raising the pH of the solution in which the synaptic vesicles are suspended increases the rate of acetylcholine uptake. Furthermore, transport is inhibited when drugs are added that make the membrane permeable to H+ ions. Which of the following set of statements are consistent with the observation?
i. Acetylcholine is being transported into the vesicle by H+-acetylcholine antiport system.
ii. H+ gradient that drives the uptake is generated by an ATP driven H+ pump.
iii. Raising the pH of the solution surrounding the vesicles increases the H+ gradient.
iv. Transport of acetylcholine into the vesicle is a secondary active transport process.
why: ATP is needed to run a proton pump that makes the vesicle interior acidic. Acetylcholine enters in exchange for H+ (antiport, secondary active transport). A higher pH outside means a bigger H+ difference across the membrane, so uptake rises; H+-leaking drugs destroy the gradient and inhibit it. All four fit.

q:
A Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) with all the required components including the 'Forward' and 'Reverse' primers results in ~ 1 billion copies of double stranded DNA molecules after 30 cycles of optimized thermal cycling programme.
A research scholar designed PCR primers to amplify a 300 bp region of the gyrA gene from genomic DNA of E. coli. During the PCR reaction set up, he forgot to add the 'Reverse' primer in the PCR reaction mixture. Which of the following is correct?
why: With only the forward primer, polymerase extends it along the template, but there is no reverse primer to mark the 300 bp end, so it runs on to the end of the template, giving linear (not exponential) single-stranded products longer than 300 nt.
opts: The DNA polymerization will not take place at all, and thus there will be no new DNA copies synthesized.
The DNA strand complementary to the 'Forward' primer will be synthesized during every cycle of PCR and therefore only half a billion copies of the 300 bp target amplicon will be formed.
Only arithmetic increase in the copy number of complementary strand of the 'Forward primer' will take place, resulting in 300 bp single-stranded DNA molecules.
Single stranded DNA fragments longer than the intended 300 bp would be synthesized during DNA polymerization.

q: An experiment was carried out where plants were grown in soils with varying water potentials and the various physiological changes were monitored. If the water potential is varied from -1 to -3 MPa then absicissic acid accumulation; cell expansion and stomatal conductance would respectively:
why: As soil water potential drops (more water stress), ABA builds up, which closes stomata (conductance falls), and turgor-driven cell expansion decreases.

q:
The success of the early green revolution was largely due to:
i. semi-dwarf varieties, that put more energy into seed production than vegetative growth, were introduced.
ii. genetically modified high-yielding varieties were introduced.
iii. use of chemical fertilizers was increased.
iv. genetically modified disease resistant varieties were introduced.
why: The early green revolution relied on conventionally bred semi-dwarf varieties plus heavy fertiliser use; genetically modified crops came much later, which rules out ii and iv.

q: All aquatic animals whether marine, brackish or freshwater need to regulate their internal osmotic potential against the external one. Although the standard Na+/K+-ATPase pump operates at the basolateral cell membranes in these animals, the kinetic properties can vary based on the environment. Which of the following is true about the Km (concentration for half maximal transport) for this enzyme?
why: Freshwater has very little Na+, so the pump must grab sodium efficiently at low concentration; a low Km means high affinity, which fits freshwater animals.
opts: Km values in marine invertebrates are likely to be higher than fresh water invertebrates indicating high affinity for the pump.
The enzyme in freshwater invertebrates is likely to show higher Km values indicating low affinity for the pump.
The enzyme in marine invertebrates is likely to show lower Km values indicating higher affinity for the pump.
The enzyme in freshwater invertebrates is likely to show lower Km values indicating higher affinity for the pump.

q: While rushing to the exam hall you fall and hurt your leg. You vigorously rub the affected area and feel less pain. This is because:
why: This is the gate-control idea: touch and pressure signals from rubbing compete with pain signals in the spinal cord and reduce the transmission of pain, rather than directly silencing the pain receptors.
opts: Rubbing the affected area releases analgesics (pain inhibitors) from the skin, which acts on the pain receptors.
Vigorous rubbing opens mechanically-gated Cl- channels on the sensory neurons causing Cl- influx, which causes hyperpolarization of the sensory neurons.
Vigorous rubbing desensitizes pain receptors at the affected area.
Vigorous rubbing at the affected area generates multiple alternative impulses which act as competing sensory information.

q:
The glomerular filtration rate (GFR) can be determined through the direct measurement of the clearance of exogenous substances, such as inulin, injected into the body. Alternatively, it can be indirectly calculated by evaluating the clearance of endogenous substances like creatinine. In primates, including humans, there is a certain amount of creatinine secretion and/or reabsorption in kidney tubules, which is absent in non-primate mammals. Which of the following statements are correct?
i. The measurement of clearance of creatinine can be employed for the precise assessment of GFR in humans.
ii. The measurement of clearance of inulin can be employed for the precise assessment of GFR in humans.
iii. The measurement of clearance of creatinine can be employed for the precise estimation of GFR in non-primate mammals.
iv. The measurement of clearance of inulin can be employed for the precise assessment of GFR in non-primate mammals.
v. Measurement of clearance of inulin will be less accurate than creatinine as inulin is not produced by the body.
why: Inulin is filtered but neither secreted nor reabsorbed, so it measures GFR precisely in any mammal. Creatinine is handled by the tubules in primates (so it is imprecise in humans) but not in non-primates, where it is precise.

q:
The freshwater environment can be classified into two natural divisions namely lentic (standing water bodies) and lotic (running water bodies). In lotic habitat with rapid streams, several body adaptations can be observed in animals. A few are listed below. Which of these apply to lotic habitat?
i. Body with hooks and suckers
ii. Sticky dorsal surfaces
iii. Positive thigmotaxy (response of an animal to contact or touch)
iv. Negative rheotaxy (response to oncoming current)
v. Streamlined body
why: Animals in fast streams resist being washed away by clinging (hooks, suckers, positive thigmotaxy) and by a streamlined shape. Sticky dorsal surfaces are not an adaptation, and they show positive (not negative) rheotaxy, facing the current.

q: What are the three essential requirements for natural selection to occur?
why: Natural selection needs variation, heritability of that variation, and differential survival or reproduction; population size and sexual reproduction are not essential.
opts: Large population sizes, variation in traits, differential survival and/or reproduction.
Large population sizes, heritability of traits, sexual reproduction.
Variation in traits, heritability of traits, differential survival and/or reproduction.
Sexual reproduction, variation in traits, heritability of traits.

q: In plants, Cytoplasmic Male Sterility (CMS) arises due to mutations in the mitochondrial genome. In many cases it has been found that male fertility can be restored by nuclear encoded fertility restorer (Rf) gene. Lines that can restore CMS are called fertility restorer lines. A cross is made between a CMS and Rf line. All progeny produced are male fertile. If the progeny is selfed, what percentage of the progeny will be male fertile?
why: The F1 plants have CMS cytoplasm and are heterozygous (Rf/rf). On selfing, 3/4 of the offspring carry at least one Rf allele and are fertile; only rf/rf (1/4) is sterile.

q: Attenuation is a regulatory mechanism in tryptophan operon that results in premature termination of transcription. Such mechanism is not possible in an eukaryote because:
why: Attenuation depends on a ribosome translating the leader peptide while RNA polymerase is still transcribing. In eukaryotes transcription (nucleus) and translation (cytoplasm) are separated, so this coupling cannot occur.
opts: transcription and translation are not coupled.
sigma factor is not involved in transcription initiation.
Shine-Dalgarno sequence needed for ribosome recognition is absent in eukaryotic mRNA

q:
While considering the genetic basis of behaviour, there are three levels where variation can contribute to behavioural differences, namely genome composition (X), gene variants (Y) and gene expression (Z).
Consider members of the following 3 species:
(i) Drosophila simulans
(ii) Drosophila sechellia
(iii) Culex pipiens
Which of the following statements is true?
why: Members of different species (including a mosquito versus flies) differ in all three: genome composition, gene variants and expression. The other statements wrongly restrict the differences to fewer levels or assume the environment erases genetic differences.
opts: Members of (i) will differ from each other with respect to only Z.
Members of (i) and (ii) will differ from each other with respect to only Y and Z.
Members of (i), (ii) and (iii) will differ from each other with respect to X, Y and Z.
Members of (i) and (ii) will have the same X, Y and Z if they share the same environment and habitat.

q: Which of the following statements best describes evolution?
why: Mutations arise irrespective of need and drift is chance sampling, but selection favours individuals according to their fitness, so it is the non-random force.
opts: Genetic drift is a random process, but mutation and selection are non-random.
Mutation and genetic drift are random processes, but selection is non-random.
Mutation and selection are random processes, but genetic drift is non-random.
Selection is a random process, but mutation and genetic drift are non-random.

q:
In 2020, doctors used convalescent plasma therapy to treat coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19). This therapy used plasma from people who had recovered from COVID-19, which was transfused to the patient.
The following statements are made about plasma therapy:
i. Person who caught infection after being vaccinated and then recovered are likely to be better donors than those who were not vaccinated
ii. The donor's plasma should have high levels of antigen for the treatment to be effective.
iii. In plasma therapy a person with AB Rh+ blood group will be universal donor.
Which one of the following options represents all correct statements?
why: Vaccinated people who then recover have higher antibody titres (i true). The plasma needs antibodies, not antigen (ii false). AB plasma has no anti-A or anti-B antibodies, so it is the universal plasma donor (iii true).

q: Herbivores have evolved to feed effectively, while plants have countered with a wide variety of anti-herbivore defenses. Extrafloral nectar is one such defence tool which attracts diverse predators and parasitoids, especially ants. Higher volumes of extrafloral nectar production attract more ants and can increase their aggressiveness. The relationship between the plant and the ants can be correctly described as:
why: The plant provides nectar to the ants and the ants defend the plant against herbivores, so both benefit: mutualism.

q: How many molecules of CO2 need to be fixed to complete one Calvin cycle and regenerate RuBP?
why: Each CO2 fixed gives one 3-PGA via RuBisCO, and three turns (3 CO2) give one net G3P while regenerating the three RuBP (5-carbon) molecules consumed, so one complete cycle needs 3 CO2.

q: Several mechanisms have evolved in plants that avoid self-pollination. In a plant, one such mechanism is seen in the growing pollen tube. If the incompatibility gene is expressed during the development of pollen tube, the style and stigma block further growth of pollen tube. This mechanism, operative between pollen tube and style-stigma, respectively is:
why: The pollen tube is the male gametophyte and therefore haploid, while style and stigma are sporophytic maternal tissue and therefore diploid.

q: In Mirabilis plant, inheritance of leaf colour is due to plastids. If pollen grains from a variegated branch are used to pollinate the stigma of a flower from a green branch, it will result in plants with:
why: Plastid inheritance is maternal; pollen contributes essentially no plastids, so the progeny take the colour of the green seed parent.

q: Marine sponges exhibit filter feeding wherein the water is taken into their body. The cells such as archaeocytes and choanocytes (collar cells) are instrumental in the process of digesting the ingested food. The waste is removed through the outward movement of water. Which of the following correctly depicts the sequence of events during the ingestion and digestion in a sponge?
why: Water enters via the small ostia and exits through the large osculum. Choanocytes capture and digest the particles first, then pass food to the wandering archaeocytes, which distribute it to other cells.
opts: Food particles → Osculum → Archaeocytes → Choanocytes → Intracellular digestion → distributed to other cells of the body → Undigested food expelled through ostia
Food particles → Ostia → Archaeocytes → Choanocytes → Intracellular digestion → distributed to other cells of the body → Undigested food expelled through osculum
Food particles → Ostia → Choanocytes → Intracellular digestion → Archaeocytes → distributed to other cells of the body → Undigested food expelled through osculum
Food particles → Osculum → Choanocytes → Intracellular digestion → Archaeocytes → distributed to other cells of the body → Undigested food expelled through ostia

q: TONPG is a compound which is toxic to E. coli. This is transported into the cell by lactose permease, the protein encoded by lac Y gene of the lactose operon. TONPG is not cleaved by beta-galactosidase (encoded by lac Z gene). TONPG can be used to isolate mutants of the lactose operon. Which one of the following mutants can be isolated using TONPG?
why: TONPG kills only cells that import it through permease. Cells that survive on TONPG must lack functional permease, i.e. lac Y mutants (constitutive lac I or operator mutants would make more permease and die).
opts: Mutants of lac Z, which do not make beta-galactosidase.
Mutants of lac Y, which do not make permease.
Mutants of the lac I gene which do not make a functional repressor protein.
Constitutive mutants in the operator region of the lactose operon.

q: Two genotypes of a bacterial species, M and N, were found to grow at 10% (growth rate = 1.10) and 5% (growth rate = 1.05), respectively, per generation at 37 C in LB media. In an experiment, 10^3 bacterial cells of each genotype were taken together in a flask and the growth was observed for 500 generations under non-limiting nutrient conditions at 37 C in LB media. Assuming no new mutations would arise during the experiment, which one of the following statements is true regarding this experiment?
why: The ratio M:N grows as (1.10/1.05)^t, which increases without limit, so M's frequency tends to 100% and N's to 0%. Both growing does not stop this; there is no balancing force for an equilibrium, and the ratio after 500 generations is astronomically larger than 2.
opts: After 500 generations, the number cells corresponding to genotype M will be 2 times more than genotype N.
The frequency of genotype N decreases progressively and eventually; genotype M will approach 100% and genotype N will approach 0% of the total population.
Genotype M will never approach 100% and genotype N will never approach 0% as both genotypes exhibit positive growth rate of > 1.
The genotype proportions would stabilize after some generations and reach an equilibrium.

q: If volcanic eruptions take place and a land becomes barren, the correct order of succession would be:
why: On bare rock (primary succession) lichens colonise first, followed by mosses, then shrubs, trees and finally the climax community; the other options skip stages or start with the wrong pioneers.
opts: Lichens → Bryophytes → Shrubs → Trees → Climax community.
Shrubs → Small trees → Biggers trees → Climax community.

q:
Solbrig and Simpson carried out a study on dandelion (Taraxacum officinale) over four years. The characteristic feature of this weed is that it produces seeds apomictically (without sexual reproduction). Therefore, in any given locality, the genetic lines present are few and each lineage is a clone of one genetic type. They identified four genetic types, P, Q, R and S, on 3 grasslands situated close to each other. These grasslands were facing different amounts of disturbances. The following table shows different proportions of the four genetic lines present at each site.
Habitat 1 (trampled, dry grassland mown every week, bare ground patches): P 73, Q 13, R 15, S 0
Habitat 2 (moderately trampled, mown every week, in shade): P 53, Q 32, R 14, S 1
Habitat 3 (wet, shaded, mown once a year): P 17, Q 8, R 11, S 64
Which genetic type of dandelions is most likely to be a K-selected population?
why: K-selected types do best in stable, crowded, undisturbed habitats. Type S dominates only the least disturbed site (mown once a year), while P thrives where disturbance is frequent (r-type).

q: In an old Sherlock Holmes movie, a criminal kept a 12.5 cm long knife (mass 1 kg), in a 15 cm thick book (excluding thickness of the covers) with a spring trap. The spring has 25 turns each of 1 mm thickness. The spring is fixed at the back cover and the knife presses the spring to its maximum when the front cover is closed so that the turns touch each other. The design is such that if the book is held in front of the body and opened, the knife gets detached from the spring and hits the reader (Sherlock Holmes in this case). Unstretched length of the spring is equal to thickness of the book. However, Sherlock Holmes was too smart and hence he opened the book in such a way that the knife flew vertically upwards. All the energy of the spring is given to the knife, which just reached the ceiling, at a height of 5 m from the tip of the knife and got stuck there. Calculate the spring constant which satisfies the equation F = - kx.
why: The fully compressed spring is 25 mm long and the free length is 150 mm, so the compression is 125 mm. Spring energy (1/2)k x^2 equals the knife's gain in potential energy m g h = 1 x 10 x 5 = 50 J, which gives k = 6400 N/m = 6.4 N/mm.

q: A black dot has a mass of about one femto gram. Assuming that the dot is made up of carbon only, calculate the approximate number of carbon atoms present in the dot.
why: One femtogram is 10^-15 g. Dividing by 12 g/mol gives about 8 x 10^-17 mol, and multiplying by 6 x 10^23 atoms/mol gives about 5 x 10^7 atoms.

q: Among the following, the third ionisation energy is highest for which one of the following elements?
why: Removing a third electron from beryllium means breaking into the stable 1s2 inner core after its two valence electrons are gone, which costs far more energy than removing a third valence-shell electron from B, Mg or Al.

q: In a hypothetical situation, a cell was found to lack rough endoplasmic reticulum. Which one of the following activities was all likely absent in this cell?
why: Rough ER carries the ribosomes that make proteins destined for secretion. Transcription happens in the nucleus, free ribosomes still translate, and lipids are made by smooth ER, so only secretory protein synthesis would be lost.
opts: Manufacture of fat molecules or lipids

q: In liver transplantation, the first three months after transplantation is when the patient requires the most care and post-surgery monitoring. Which of the following statement is most suitable up to three months for a patient who has undergone liver-transplantation recently?
why: The body would reject the foreign organ, so immunosuppressants are needed, but suppressing immunity leaves the patient open to infection, so antibiotics are given as well.
opts: She will require no drugs but only care and follow ups.
She will be treated with immunosuppressive drugs only.
She will be treated with antibiotics only.
She will be treated with combination of immunosuppressive drugs and antibiotics.

q: While driving on a level road at 72 kmph, Vinayak observes the traffic signal turning red, the (white) stopping line being 52 m away from the front end of his car. Immediately he applies the brakes that decelerate his car at 4 m/s2. How far from the stopping line will the front end of Vinayak's car be after 6 seconds?
why: 72 km/h is 20 m/s, so the car stops after 5 s and does not move after that. The stopping distance is 20^2/(2 x 4) = 50 m, leaving the front end 2 m short of the line.

q: When a mixture of 60mL of carbon monoxide and 40mL of oxygen is sparked, mixture A is obtained. Mixture A is passed through aqueous potassium hydroxide to yield mixture B. The volumes of mixtures A and B respectively are
why: 2CO + O2 -> 2CO2, so 60 mL CO uses 30 mL O2 and gives 60 mL CO2, leaving 10 mL O2: mixture A is 70 mL. KOH absorbs the CO2, leaving only the 10 mL of oxygen as mixture B.

q: A convex mirror of radius of curvature 12 cm has its principal axis horizontal. A simple pendulum with a tiny bob is oscillating in front of the mirror such that centre of mass of the bob is 12 cm away from the mirror along the principal axis. Amplitude of oscillation is 3 cm and there is practically no damping. Length of the pendulum is sufficiently large and the plane of oscillation is such that the bob moves practically along the principal axis of the mirror. Path length of the image of the bob formed by the mirror is …..
why: The focal length is 6 cm and the object distance swings between 9 cm and 15 cm. Using the mirror formula the image distance is 3.6 cm at u = 9 cm and about 4.29 cm at u = 15 cm, so the image moves over a stretch of about 0.7 cm.

q: Choose the correct sequence of the following ions in increasing order of their ionic radii.
why: Be2+ and Li+ have 2 electrons, and the higher nuclear charge makes Be2+ smaller. F- and O2- have 10 electrons, and the lower nuclear charge makes O2- larger than F-. Cations are smaller than anions.

q: A compound exists in the gaseous state both as monomer (A) and dimer (A2). The molecular weight of the monomer is 48. In an experiment, 96 g of the compound was confined in a vessel of volume 33.6 litres and heated to 273 deg C. Calculate the pressure developed, if the compound exists as a dimer to the extent of 50% by weight under this condition, assuming that temperature does not affect the physical state of the dimer.
why: 48 g exists as monomer (1 mol) and 48 g as dimer A2 of mass 96 (0.5 mol), so the total is 1.5 mol of gas. P = nRT/V = 1.5 x 0.082 x 546 / 33.6 = 2 atm.

q:
Following are some statements about mitochondria and chloroplasts:
I. Mitochondrion has double stranded DNA that replicates independently while chloroplast does not have the same.
II. Both mitochondria and chloroplast have double stranded DNA that replicates independently.
III. Both mitochondria and chloroplast have single stranded DNA replicating independently.
IV. Mitochondria and chloroplast have both RNA and ribosomes.
Which of the above statements are correct?
why: Both organelles are semi-autonomous: each has its own circular double-stranded DNA that replicates on its own, and each has RNA and ribosomes for making some proteins. That makes II and IV correct.

q: A solution of pure ferric sulphate containing 0.140g of ferric ions is treated with excess of barium hydroxide solution. Total weight of the precipitate will be.
why: 0.140 g Fe3+ is 0.0025 mol, giving 0.0025 mol Fe(OH)3 (0.27 g). Ferric sulphate has 3 sulphate per 2 Fe, so 0.00375 mol BaSO4 (0.87 g) also precipitates. The total is about 1.14 g.

q:
Fishes such as Salmon are called as anadromous fish. They are born in fresh water. However, then they migrate to the sea and spend most of their life in the sea. They return to fresh water to spawn. On the contrary, catadromous fishes such as Eels do the opposite. They live in fresh water for their entire life. They migrate to the sea to spawn.
Which one of the following strategies will Salmon adopt in order to manage the problem of osmoregulation when it is in the sea?
why: In sea water the fish loses water to the saltier surroundings, so it must drink a lot to replace it (and excrete the excess salt), whereas in fresh water it gains water and hardly needs to drink.
opts: Salmon drinks profusely in sea and it drinks feebly in fresh water.
It produces large volume of dilute urine in sea water.
In sea water, gills filter NaCl which is absorbed selectively into its body.
The mode of excretion of Salmon is changed from ammonia to uric acid.

q:
You are provided with 4 metal ores at different levels of activity series, extraction of these metals from their ores involves oxidation and reductions. Match the metal ores with their extraction processes.
Metal ores: 1. Cinnabar, 2. Zincblende, 3. Hematite, 4. Galena
Processes: I. Oxidation and reduction, II. Oxidation, III. Electrolysis, IV. Reduction
why: Cinnabar (HgS) is roasted in air and mercury comes off directly (oxidation). Zinc blende and galena are roasted to oxides and then reduced (oxidation and reduction). Hematite is an oxide, so it only needs reduction.

q: In a hypothetical experiment the outer tissues of the woody part of the stem of a dicotyledonous plant is removed in the form of a ring, leaving only the xylem and pith intact. Which one of the statements is most likely to be correct?
why: Xylem carries water upward and is left intact. The removed outer tissue includes the phloem, which carries food down from the leaves, so food movement stops at the ring.
opts: Water transport from the root to leaves will be obstructed but food transport from leaves to stem will be unhindered.
Water transport from root to leaves will not be obstructed but food transport from stem to leaves will be hindered.
Water transport from root to leaves will not be obstructed but food transport down the leaves stops at the ring.
Water transport from leaves to root is obstructed but food transport down from the leaves stops at the ring.

q:
Bones, ligaments and muscles are structures that are considered to be lever system in the body for human movement. Classically, the levers are represented as: first, second and third (I, II and III), classes of levers depending on their relative positions of the fulcrum, effort and resistance (or load).
Given below are few body part movements (represented as P = backward bending of neck, Q = walking on toe and R = folding of arm) which can be compared to specific classes of levers. From the options below identify the correct combination of body part to that of a class of lever.
why: Bending the neck back works like a first-class lever (fulcrum between effort and load), standing on the toes is a second-class lever (load between fulcrum and effort), and folding the arm at the elbow is a third-class lever (effort between fulcrum and load).

q: If 22 g of nitrogen gas, 44 g of oxygen gas and 38 g of carbon dioxide gas are kept in separate containers at the same temperature and volume, then what will be the order of their pressure?
why: At fixed T and V pressure is proportional to the number of moles: N2 = 22/28 = 0.79 mol, CO2 = 38/44 = 0.86 mol, O2 = 44/32 = 1.375 mol. So N2 < CO2 < O2.

q: Which one of the following statements is true about the fate of glucose, following oxidation in the presence and in the absence of oxygen?
why: Without oxygen, fermentation follows glycolysis (ethanol in yeast, for example), and with oxygen pyruvate is converted to acetyl-CoA inside the mitochondria. Only option (b) has the acetyl-CoA step in the right place with a valid fermentation product.
opts: In absence of oxygen, glucose undergoes only up to glycolysis and pyruvate is converted to lactate, while in the presence of oxygen glucose undergoes only up to glycolysis and pyruvate is converted to acetyl-CoA in the cytosol.

In absence of oxygen, glucose undergoes only up to glycolysis and pyruvate is converted to ethanol, while in the presence of oxygen glucose undergoes only up to glycolysis and pyruvate is converted to acetyl-CoA in the mitochondria.

In absence of oxygen glucose undergoes only up to glycolysis and pyruvate is converted to acetyl-CoA, while in the presence of oxygen glucose undergoes only up to glycolysis and pyruvate is converted to lactate in the muscle.

In absence of oxygen glucose undergoes only up to glycolysis and pyruvate is converted to lactate, while in the presence of oxygen glucose undergoes only up to glycolysis and pyruvate is converted to ethanol in bacterial cell.

q:
Following experiments were carried out separately in chemistry laboratory in different test tubes, labelled as (I), (II), (III), and (IV).
(I) Mg + dil. HCl
(II) Al + dil. H2SO4
(III) Cu + dil. HCl
(IV) Mn + dil. HNO3
She observed hydrogen gas is not produced in:
why: Mg, Al and Mn are above hydrogen in the reactivity series and release H2 from dilute acids (Mn gives H2 even with very dilute nitric acid), but copper is below hydrogen and does not react with dilute HCl.

q: An astronaut has to burn 40g of glucose in his body per hour to get the required energy. Find the amount of oxygen that would need to be carried in space to meet his energy requirement for thirty days.
why: In 30 days he burns 40 x 720 = 28.8 kg glucose. C6H12O6 + 6O2 needs 192 g of O2 per 180 g of glucose, so oxygen needed = 28.8 x 192/180 = 30.7 kg.

q:
A particle moves along positive X-axis with a velocity (in a suitable unit) varying as (4 - 3t - t^2) where t is time in seconds. Students draw following four conclusions.
(I) Initially the particle is at the origin.
(II) Initial speed of the particle is zero.
(III) The particle decelerates till t = 1 s.
(IV) The speed of the particle goes on increasing after t = 1 s.
Therefore, conclusions
why: At t = 0 the velocity is 4, so the initial speed is never zero, ruling out (II). The starting position is not given, so (I) holds only sometimes. Velocity falls to zero at t = 1 s (slowing down), then becomes negative with growing magnitude (speeding up).
opts: (i) & (ii) are sometimes correct, (iii) & (iv) are always correct
